draft.title: Tap-target + slip-adjacency sweep
draft.principle_summary: Two separate, non-overlapping authorities govern interactive-target geometry. WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) is a Level AA success criterion added in WCAG 2.2 (not 2.1): pointer targets must be at least 24x24 CSS px, or, if smaller, have their center at least 24px from any adjacent target's center, with five named exceptions (inline text targets, essential, user-agent-controlled, equivalent target available). WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced) is a separate, stricter Level AAA criterion: 44x44 CSS px, no spacing escape hatch. Apple HIG independently sets a 44x44pt hit-region floor for buttons (60x60pt on visionOS). Material Design sets 48x48dp with an 8dp recommended minimum spacing between adjacent targets. All four numbers trace to the same mechanic, Fitts's Law (index of difficulty falls as target width W rises), reinforced by fingertip contact-patch data (roughly 7 to 9mm, close to 44px at typical mobile density). A second, distinct mechanic not covered by target size alone is slip adjacency: when two adjacent targets carry very different consequences (confirm vs destroy, Bezahlen vs Abbrechen), the risk is not "can this be tapped" but "can this be tapped BY MISTAKE instead of its neighbor," a function of inter-target distance and consequence asymmetry, not raw size. No mainstream tool checks slip adjacency; axe-core's target-size rule checks only the WCAG 2.5.8 geometry.

draft.solen_current:
Solen already has substantial coverage, spread across three files, none of it wired into a running check:

1. RATIONALE.md:157 (Domain 5, "Target sizes"): "WCAG 2.5.8 AA (2.2) 24x24 CSS px minimum; WCAG 2.5.5 AAA 44x44; Apple HIG 44pt; Material 48dp with 8dp spacing. Solen's 44px floor (design contract) is the AAA/HIG line, deliberately above the legal AA minimum." This is already correctly tiered T1 and already distinguishes AA from AAA. It is NOT the conflated line the key_question points at.

2. SOURCE.md:1032 (section 16.5, Touch targets), the actual conflation the key_question names: "Minimum 44x44 px hit area per WCAG 2.1 (some platforms 48)." This is wrong on two counts: (a) WCAG 2.1 has no 44x44 requirement at any conformance level that Solen ships against (2.1's own Target Size, SC 2.5.5, is AAA only, and Solen's AA-target conformance would not require it even at 2.1), and (b) the criterion that actually gates AA conformance today is 2.5.8 at 24x24, introduced in WCAG 2.2, not 2.1. SOURCE.md presents a design-contract choice (44px) as if it were a legal AA floor, which overstates the mandate and hides that Solen is voluntarily choosing the AAA/HIG number over the AA minimum.

3. RATIONALE.md:221 (Domain 10, touch ergonomics, "Slip adjacency"): "two targets whose consequences differ wildly (Bezahlen vs Abbrechen) need more than 8px separation or a size/prominence asymmetry; the mechanic is touch landing scatter (~7-9mm typical fingertip contact), which is also why 44px ~ 9mm is the floor." Tiered T2. This is the qualitative rule; it has never been turned into a script.

4. research/GEOMETRY_PRINCIPLES_2026-07-17.md:83-91, 165-175, 266-281 already specs axe-core's target-size rule as the CI check that closes gap-register D6 for the WCAG 2.5.8 half (24x24 + 24px-separation geometry), naming @axe-core/playwright, the exact Deque rule text, and where to wire it (e2e/visual/spine.spec.ts). It explicitly notes this covers ONLY the standards-mandated 24x24 floor, not Solen's own stricter 44px design-contract floor, and not slip adjacency at all: "outside touch-target size, no mainstream tool checks off-grid spacing, axis alignment, or symmetry."

Gap-register: RATIONALE.md:844, row D6, "Tap-target + slip-adjacency sweep (44px floor, 8px consequential separation, computed per screen)," marked "YES" (mechanizable) but still unbuilt as of this research pass.
draft.gap:
Three distinct gaps, all closeable without touching any locked literal:

GAP 1 (bare-citation error, correctable text, not a locked value): SOURCE.md:1032 cites "WCAG 2.1" for a 44x44 floor that WCAG 2.1 never mandates at AA, and omits that the actual AA-mandated number today is 24x24 under 2.5.8 (WCAG 2.2). This is a documentation-accuracy fix, not a re-opening of the 44px design-contract value itself (that value is locked and correct, just mis-cited). Fix: replace "per WCAG 2.1 (some platforms 48)" with the same accurate framing RATIONALE.md:157 already uses (44px = the AAA/HIG line, chosen above the AA 24px minimum), and point SOURCE §16.5 at RATIONALE domain 5/10 instead of restating a wrong citation.

GAP 2 (D6 marked mechanizable, never built): axe-core's target-size rule (GEOMETRY_PRINCIPLES §4) closes only the standards half (WCAG 2.5.8 geometry: 24x24 or 24px separation). It does not enforce Solen's own stricter 44px design-contract floor (axe-core would pass a 24px control that Solen's own contract fails), and it has no concept of slip adjacency (differing-consequence pairs) at all, since WCAG 2.5.8's spacing exception treats ALL nearby targets identically regardless of what they do.

GAP 3 (no tool anywhere checks slip adjacency): this is the net-new half of D6 that dedup_notes flags explicitly ("axe-core target-size rule already documented in GEOMETRY tooling; D6 adds slip-adjacency, which no tool checks"). Nothing in Solen's stack, or in any mainstream a11y tool, currently computes "is a destructive control too close to a benign one." This needs its own metric, distinct from raw target-size checking, because it needs a semantic input (which controls are "consequential" and which pairs are "adjacent-but-different-consequence") that no DOM-geometry tool can infer on its own.
draft.proposed_addition:
COMPUTABLE METRIC SPEC: Tap-target-floor + slip-adjacency sweep (closes gap-register D6, RATIONALE.md:844)

Two sub-checks, run together against a rendered route (Playwright, same infra as e2e/visual/spine.spec.ts and GEOMETRY_PRINCIPLES §4/§5).

CHECK A: Solen-floor target-size sweep (extends the standards-only axe-core check to Solen's own stricter contract)

Inputs, per interactive element on the rendered page (button, link, input, any element with a role of button/link/checkbox/radio/tab, or an onClick handler):
- rect = element.getBoundingClientRect() (the unobscured hit area; if a larger invisible hit-slop wrapper exists, e.g. HeartButton's 44 outer / 32 inner pattern, measure the OUTER hit element, not the painted glyph)
- w = rect.width, h = rect.height
- exempt = true if the element is inline text inside a text block (WCAG 2.5.8 inline-target exception) OR is in a named, dated Solen exception list (e.g. TabPill 32/40px, FeaturedStylists SaveHeart 28x28, both already recorded as documented SACRIFICES in RATIONALE.md:485-486, 494)

Formula and thresholds (two tiers, not one, because Solen's design contract sits above the legal floor):
- BLOCKING (fails WCAG 2.5.8 AA, the legal floor): min(w, h) < 24 AND no other same-type target center is >= 24px away AND not exempt
- ADVISORY (fails Solen's own 44px design-contract floor, RATIONALE.md:157 / LOCKFILE 44px row): min(w, h) < 44 AND not exempt AND not already on the named-exception list
- Output per flagged node: selector, w x h, which tier failed, nearest-neighbor distance if the spacing exception was the reason it passed/failed.

This reuses axe-core's own target-size rule (already specced in GEOMETRY_PRINCIPLES §4) for the BLOCKING tier verbatim (do not reimplement WCAG 2.5.8 math by hand, it is a solved, MIT-licensed, CI-gateable check). The ADVISORY tier is the net-new piece: a second pass at the same rects against Solen's own 44px number, which axe-core has no reason to know about.

CHECK B: Slip-adjacency sweep (net-new, closes the actual D6 delta dedup_notes flags)

Inputs:
- A CONSEQUENCE tag per interactive element, sourced from a small manual annotation, not inferred from the DOM: "commit" (primary confirm, e.g. Bezahlen, Buchen), "destructive" (delete, cancel-and-lose-progress, remove), "neutral" (everything else). Practical source: a data attribute the component sets, e.g. data-consequence="destructive", added once per component type (delete buttons, cancel-and-discard buttons, the booking commit CTA), not per instance.
- rect for every tagged element (same getBoundingClientRect as Check A)

Formula:
- For every pair (A, B) of tagged elements where A.consequence != B.consequence and at least one of {A, B} is "destructive" or "commit" (i.e. skip neutral-neutral pairs, they carry no slip cost):
  - centerDistance = euclidean distance between rect centers
  - edgeGap = shortest gap between the two bounding boxes (0 if they touch or overlap)
- FLAG if edgeGap < 24px (reuses the same WCAG 2.5.8 24px spacing constant as the separation floor, since it is the only named standards number for inter-target spacing) UNLESS a size/prominence asymmetry is present: the lower-consequence or lesser element is at least 1.5x smaller in area, OR has visibly lower prominence (this half needs a human check today, computable prominence, e.g. contrast ratio delta or fill vs outline, is a candidate future refinement, not required to ship the first version).
- Output per flagged pair: both selectors, both consequence tags, edgeGap in px, and whether a size/prominence asymmetry was detected.

What it flags in practice: a delete icon sitting 8px from a save icon in a settings row; a Bezahlen and an Abbrechen button in the same flex row with 12px gap and equal visual weight; a destructive swipe action revealed at the same distance as a neutral one. What it does NOT flag: two neutral filter chips 4px apart (no slip cost), or a destructive action that is already spatially isolated (top-right overflow menu vs a bottom-center commit CTA, per the thumb-reach zoning in RATIONALE.md domain 10).

Where it slots in: same route list as GEOMETRY_PRINCIPLES §4/§5 (search-results, salon-PDP, booking-services, plus any settings/account screen with delete actions, since that is where slip-adjacency risk concentrates). Check A's BLOCKING tier is a straight axe-core wire-in (near-zero new code). Check A's ADVISORY tier and Check B are new script logic (Check B genuinely net-new, since it needs the semantic consequence tag no existing tool has).

TASTE LAB PROBE (to calibrate the size/prominence-asymmetry threshold, the one qualitative judgment call in Check B): show 3 renders of the same delete-next-to-save control pair, varying only edgeGap (8px, 16px, 24px+) and size ratio (equal size, 1.5x, 2x), ask which pairs feel "safe to tap without looking twice." Use the answer to convert the current TBD 1.5x area-ratio guess into a locked number, the same way other unsettled probes in this file already resolve open constants.
draft.taste_lab_probe: 3-way probe: same delete-vs-save icon pair, held at 3 edge-gaps (8px, 16px, 24px+) crossed with 2 size ratios (equal, 1.5x larger commit control), asking "which pairs feel safe to tap without double-checking." Resolves the currently-guessed 1.5x size-asymmetry escape hatch in Check B into a real, sourced number instead of an assumed one.

verified.title: Tap-target + slip-adjacency sweep
myths_caught: The draft's T3 fingertip-contact-patch figure ("roughly 7 to 9mm") is a slightly-off recall of the actual MIT Touch Lab numbers (fingertip ~8-10mm, finger pad ~10-14mm); not on the myth_screen table itself (that table is scoped to conversion/retention/psychology stats, not touch-ergonomics), but it fails the same reality-over-memory check and needed correction to the real range with an actual named source rather than an unsourced approximation.

claim_verdicts.claim: WCAG 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum), Level AA, introduced in WCAG 2.2: pointer targets at least 24x24 CSS px, or the 24px center-distance spacing exception.
claim_verdicts.note: Confirmed against W3C Understanding docs and corroborating third-party summaries (TestParty, EqualWeb). Magnitude and conformance level are correct.

claim_verdicts.claim: WCAG 2.5.8 has five named exceptions (inline text targets, essential, user-agent-controlled, equivalent target available).
claim_verdicts.note: The count of 5 is right (Spacing, Equivalent, Inline, User Agent Controlled, Essential per the W3C SC text) but the draft's parenthetical only names 4 of the 5, it omits 'Spacing' as a named item since it treats spacing as the alternate compliance path rather than an exception. Cosmetic omission, not a magnitude error; worth a one-word fix in the addition but does not change any number used downstream.

claim_verdicts.claim: WCAG 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), Level AAA: custom targets at least 44x44 CSS px, no spacing exception, distinct and stricter criterion from 2.5.8.
claim_verdicts.note: Confirmed. Correctly distinguished from 2.5.8 as AAA not AA, which is exactly the conflation error the addition is meant to fix in SOURCE.md.

claim_verdicts.claim: Apple HIG: a button needs a hit region of at least 44x44pt (60x60pt on visionOS).
claim_verdicts.note: Verified verbatim against developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/buttons search result: 'a button needs a hit region of at least 44 x 44 pt, in visionOS, 60 x 60 pt.' Exact match.

claim_verdicts.claim: axe-core (v4.5+) ships a target-size rule implementing WCAG 2.5.8, runnable via @axe-core/playwright, off by default until the WCAG 2.2 ruleset is enabled.
claim_verdicts.note: Confirmed the target-size rule was introduced in axe-core 4.5.0 (Deque's own 4.5 release blog, corroborated by Rocket Validator's rule docs). Draft undersold one operational detail worth adding: the rule is OFF by default and needs the WCAG 2.2 ruleset explicitly enabled, otherwise a CI wire-in that assumes default-on will silently no-op. That is itself a slip-adjacency-style silent no-op risk worth flagging in the addition.

claim_verdicts.claim: Material Design sets an 8dp minimum recommended spacing between adjacent 48dp touch targets.
claim_verdicts.note: Consistent with long-standing, widely corroborated Material guidance and the project's own prior citation at RATIONALE.md:157. Not independently re-verified against a live Material spec page this pass, kept at T2 since it is corroborated by Solen's own prior citation rather than a fresh primary read.

claim_verdicts.claim: Touch landing scatter for a typical fingertip contact patch is roughly 7 to 9mm.
claim_verdicts.note: Refuted at the specific magnitude. MIT Touch Lab (the actual named study behind most fingertip-size claims) puts the FINGERTIP at roughly 8-10mm and the finger PAD at roughly 10-14mm, not 7-9mm. The draft's number is a memory-blurred approximation, not a transcription of a real source. Corrected to 8-10mm with the MIT Touch Lab attribution, kept T3 (directional grounding for why ~44px approximates a fingertip, not a precise engineering constant).

claim_verdicts.claim: 44px design-contract floor sits deliberately above the WCAG AA 24px minimum, at the AAA/HIG line.
claim_verdicts.note: Internally consistent with the now-verified 2.5.8 (24px AA) vs 2.5.5 (44px AAA) distinction and the verified 44pt Apple HIG figure. This framing (already used correctly at RATIONALE.md:157) is the fix that should replace the wrong WCAG 2.1 citation at SOURCE.md:1032.

claim_verdicts.claim: 24px slip-adjacency edge-gap floor (proposed, reuses WCAG 2.5.8's spacing constant).
claim_verdicts.note: This is an explicit design proposal borrowing a real number (WCAG 2.5.8's 24px), not a claim about the world. Correctly framed as proposed/reasoned in the draft, not asserted as an external finding. No refutation needed beyond noting it is an analogy, not a validated slip-adjacency threshold; flagged in residual_risks.
Already explicitly marked TBD/guessed in the draft and routed to a Taste Lab probe rather than asserted as fact. No refutation needed, this is honest about its own uncertainty.

verified.residual_risks:
Three items an owner should weigh, none of which touch a frozen literal:

1. The 24px slip-adjacency edge-gap floor in Check B is a borrowed constant (WCAG 2.5.8's spacing number), not a validated slip-adjacency threshold in its own right. No standard or study measures "how far apart must a destroy-button and a commit-button be to avoid accidental taps." Treat Check B's flags as advisory heuristics pending the Taste Lab probe, never a hard CI gate, until the probe grounds it or the owner accepts the borrowed number as good enough.

2. axe-core's target-size rule ships OFF by default and needs the WCAG 2.2 ruleset explicitly enabled. This is a real silent-no-op risk if whoever wires Check A into CI assumes the default axe run already covers it, worth a QUESTIONS.md or GEOMETRY_PRINCIPLES.md note so the eventual implementer does not ship a check that always reports zero findings.

3. Check A's ADVISORY tier (44px) will flag every element already on Solen's own documented exception list (TabPill 32/40px, SaveHeart 28x28) unless that exception list is kept in sync with the sweep's exempt-list input. This is a maintenance dependency, not a design question, but worth naming so the sweep does not become noisy and get ignored the way un-triaged linters often do.
